 Cash-Strapped China Tightens Grip On Offshore Wealth As Tax Compliance Deadline For Millionaires And Billionaires Ends
 Swarajya Staff
 Oct 22, 2026 | Updated 09:45 AM GMT+5:30
 Save & read from anywhere!
 Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app .
 Sign In Prefer Prefer Chinese Yuan currency notes China's wealthiest citizens face a critical deadline today (22 October) as a 90-day grace period expires for declaring and paying taxes on offshore trust income.
 Regulations announced in July levy a tax of 20 per cent on dividends and interest gained from offshore trusts, marking Beijing's most aggressive move yet to reclaim vast fortunes held overseas by the country's millionaires and billionaires.
 The new rules , issued jointly by China's Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration on 24 July, treat a resident individual's transfer of property into an offshore trust as a taxable deemed disposal . 
 The law has prompted a flurry of activity in recent weeks for China's wealthiest individuals and families to sort out their financial affairs, with many forced to liquidate assets to meet the new tax obligations.
 The measures come at an uncertain time for the Chinese economy, as local governments that once relied on land sales for revenue face cash shortages amid a years-long property crisis. 
 In 2025, the official general public budget deficit reached RMB 5.66 trillion ($793.9 billion)—more than doubling since 2019, with a projected 2026 deficit of RMB 5.89 trillion ($853.6 billion), marking the highest deficit level recorded in China's general public budget.
 The crackdown closes a longstanding loophole used by wealthy families for asset protection and succession planning. 
 Chinese offshore wealth is reported to amount to hundreds of billions of dollars – money Beijing is eager to leverage. 
 Rapid economic growth in recent decades has created legions of super-rich, many holding fortunes in trusts across Hong Kong, Singapore, Tokyo and beyond.
 Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group's China team, said China's fiscal burden will ensure that the enforcement of new overseas taxes will be sustained, adding that personal income tax will be "increasingly important" as a source of revenue. 
 Individuals who transferred assets into offshore trusts between 2023 and 2025 were granted a 90-day period to declare these holdings and settle the tax due, with income generated before 2026 allowed to be reported under a simplified structure during the same grace period. 
 Those who fail to comply by today face penalties and increased scrutiny from tax authorities.
